anchors.basis: product as placed on market; dry sample, calculated as Al
anchors.product_scope: baked foods (bread, pastries, cakes, biscuits, cookies, crackers); deep-fried flour products; batter, breading, and frying powder
anchors.notes: GB 2760-2024 National Food Safety Standard for the Uses of Food Additives (in force 2025-02-08; supersedes GB 2760-2014). Finished-product aluminium residue limit 100 mg/kg (dry sample; as Al) governing the permitted aluminium additives (potassium/ammonium aluminium sulfate INS 522/523); China banned sodium aluminium phosphate INS 541 in 2014. Additive-agnostic total-aluminium residue cap. Corroborated by Codex GSFA CXS 192-1995 use-levels-as-Al for crackers (07.1.2) and ordinary bakery (07.1.3) both 100 mg/kg. Primary-verified 2026-08-10.

cells.scope_note: Coffee as a dry commodity: green and roasted Coffea arabica and canephora beans, ground coffee, single-serve pods and capsules assessed on the coffee fill rather than the hardware, and instant or freeze-dried coffee solids. A mushroom coffee or any coffee carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16 by the taxonomy boundary rule. Coffee-flavoured dairy and plant beverages route to Category 24 or the plant-milk rows respectively. Hong Kong Cap 132V writes the product-form split for this commodity itself, setting Coffee beans at 500 ug/kg lead in the as-sold basis and Coffee beverages at 200 ug/kg in the as-consumed basis under its Note 11; HMTc preserves the split. An applicant selling canned or bottled ready-to-drink coffee is assessed on that product form in the as-consumed liquid basis against the 200 ug/kg beverage cell; an applicant selling beans, grounds, pods or instant solids is assessed in this row's dry basis. Neither number is converted into the other basis, and no brew-strength or extraction factor is invented in either direction. The capsule or pod hardware itself is a food-contact article and is governed by Category 9, not here.
